# ADR-0005: Edits as gestures; renderer reads a snapshot

> **Status:** accepted | **Date:** 2026-07-29

**References:** [RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md), [RFC-0002:C-MEMORY](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-memory), [RFC-0006:C-RENDER](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-render), [RFC-0007:C-EDIT](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-edit), [RFC-0007:C-EXTRACT](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-extract), [RFC-0007:C-INVALIDATION](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-invalidation), [RFC-0007:C-OVERVIEW](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-overview)

## Context

Manual correction is most of what a point cloud workbench is used for: lasso a region and reclassify
it, delete strays, fix ground the classifier got wrong. It is also the thing an immutable lazy
pipeline appears unable to express, and it is CloudCompare's actual value — CloudCompare simply
mutates an in-memory buffer, which is unavailable here by construction.

The obvious representations all fail. Rewriting the source is impossible for a remote COPC and
destroys the original for a local one, since COPC nodes are LAZ-compressed chunks whose modification
means recompression and hierarchy rewriting. Materialising the edited cloud abandons out-of-core
entirely. Storing per-point overrides requires a stable per-point identifier, which neither LAS nor
COPC provides.

Graphite suggested the way out. It treats the document *as* a graph and records brush strokes
parametrically rather than as pixels, so a gesture becomes data fed to a node. Its layer stack is a
projection of the graph rather than a separate model, which matters because the users here are
foresters and not node-graph people. Applied to point clouds the fit is immediate, and
[RFC-0007:C-OVERVIEW](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-overview) states the resulting shape in its compact form. Two properties of it are what made
this the answer rather than merely an attractive idea. It needs no point identity at all, because a polygon
survives reprojection and resampling where a point reference would not. And being a spatial predicate it
composes with the octree index instead of fighting it.

Graphite also supplies the warning. After years of development its raster tools remain experimental
and full non-destructive raster editing is unimplemented; its planned mitigation, JIT compilation, is
on hold pending Rust toolchain work. Point cloud editing is structurally the raster case rather than
the vector case — individual samples, not parametric shapes — so the unsolved part is the part that
transfers.

Three problems remained. Deselecting twelve stray returns among their neighbours is an enumeration
that no region expresses. A day of manual correction produces thousands of edits, and replaying them
per partition read makes a file progressively slower to open. And edits do not commute: "classify
region A as ground" then "delete ground in region B" depends on order where the regions overlap.

The hardest question was whether edits could be graph nodes at all.
[RFC-0006:C-RENDER](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-render) 1 forbids the render path from traversing the operator planner, yet the
renderer must show an edit immediately — which looked like a direct contradiction, and pointed toward
making edits a privileged overlay outside the graph.

Bevy resolved it. Bevy keeps an authoritative main world and a derived render world, joined at a
single one-way synchronisation point (the extract), which is the only place both are accessed;
pipelined rendering then runs frame N+1's logic concurrently with frame N's render. The renderer
never traverses the authoritative structure, so both obligations hold simultaneously.

## Decision

An edit is a node in the document graph, and the renderer consumes a derived snapshot refreshed at a
single one-way extract. The obligations are written in [RFC-0007:C-EDIT](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-edit) and
[RFC-0007:C-EXTRACT](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-extract); this ADR records only *why*.

Why **the gesture and not the points** (Graphite's move):

- **Size is independent of reach.** A fifty-vertex polygon describes a selection of any magnitude, so
  an edit is about a kilobyte whether it touched forty points or forty million.
- **It needs no point identity.** A polygon survives reprojection and resampling; a list of point
  references does not. This removes the ordinary edit case from depending on an identity the source
  formats cannot supply.
- **It composes with the index rather than fighting it.** An edit is already a spatial predicate, so
  evaluating it touches only intersecting partitions — editing is spatially sparse, and the octree
  exists to find sparse regions. The edit is therefore an ordinary bounded operator.
- **Users still see a layer stack.** Graphite's transferable lesson: the graph is the model, the
  layer and history lists are its projection. Foresters are not node-graph people.

Why an **extract boundary** (Bevy's move), which is what makes the graph viable at all:

- **It dissolves an apparent contradiction.** The renderer must show edits immediately, yet
  [RFC-0006:C-RENDER](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-render) 1 forbids it traversing the planner. A derived snapshot satisfies both,
  because the render path reads the snapshot and never the graph.
- **One-way flow is a structural guarantee.** The render path works at reduced level of detail by
  design; because it cannot write back, no camera position can change a result.
- **It permits pipelining.** The document can be edited while the previous frame is still rendering.

Where the borrowed model is **deliberately not followed**: an engine's extract copies values from a
resident world, and clears render state every frame. Neither is available here. Extract copies
*plans* — partition references and effective edit sets — and must never read point data or perform
retrieval, because it is the one place nothing may block ([RFC-0007:C-EXTRACT](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-extract) 4). Render state is
*retained* with incremental invalidation rather than cleared, since re-uploading a viewport of points
per frame is the cost this project exists to avoid ([RFC-0007:C-INVALIDATION](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-invalidation) 1).

Why only the renderer gets a snapshot: extract exists because of the frame budget, not because of the
graph. The processing pipeline is throughput-bound and reads the document graph directly, so the
boundary is built once rather than per consumer.

Why the stack is **spatially indexed**: this is the piece neither reference project supplies, and
[RFC-0007:C-INVALIDATION](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-invalidation)'s rationale sets out what it buys. Recording it as a decision matters because it
is the one part of the edit model that is not free — an index over the stack is state to maintain and
invalidate, accepted because the alternative degrades with use rather than with size.

The residual gap is acknowledged rather than closed: enumerated point-set edits remain necessary for
corrections no region expresses, and they require a point identity mechanism specified separately.

## Consequences

### Positive

Editing becomes expressible at all, which was in question. An edit is an ordinary bounded operator, so
[RFC-0002](../rfc/RFC-0002.md) applies unchanged and nothing new is needed to schedule it. Undo is removing a node and
history is the graph, so both come free. Edits reorder against processing steps, which the overlay
alternative could not express. And because the original source is never modified, the non-destructive
guarantees [RFC-0007:C-EDIT](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-edit) 5 draws out come with the model rather than having to be engineered onto it.

### Negative

The extract boundary is real machinery: retained render state, region-scoped invalidation, and the cost
bounds [RFC-0007:C-INVALIDATION](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-invalidation) 3 and 4 impose on resolving an effective edit set. Every processing
operator must tolerate an edit node appearing anywhere upstream. Two representations of the same data now
exist, so "which is authoritative" must be answered structurally rather than by convention, which is what
[RFC-0007:C-EXTRACT](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-extract) 1 and 2 do.

Enumerated point-set edits remain the one case the region model cannot serve, and they carry a dependency
on point references that the region form was designed to avoid.

### Neutral

Three drifts to watch. First, extract acquiring I/O — the most likely regression, since awaiting retrieval
there looks locally reasonable and stalls every frame. Second, render state being cleared and rebuilt
because that is what general-purpose engines do and it is simpler; here it silently reintroduces per-frame
re-upload. Third, the point-set escape hatch becoming the default because it is easier to implement than
good region tooling, which would smuggle the identity dependency into the ordinary path.

Reversal cost is moderate and asymmetric. Adding the overlay model later would mean two mutation models
rather than replacing one. Removing the extract boundary would put planner traversal back in the frame
budget, so it cannot be dropped without giving up [RFC-0006:C-RENDER](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-render).

## Alternatives Considered

### Edits are nodes in the document graph, and the renderer consumes a derived snapshot refreshed at a single one-way extract (accepted)

- **Pros:** An edit is an ordinary bounded operator — no new execution machinery, and RFC-0001 applies unchanged, Region edits need no point identity, and survive reprojection and resampling, Edit size is independent of reach: a polygon covers forty points or forty million, Undo is removing a node; history is the graph; edits reorder against processing steps, Extract satisfies [RFC-0006:C-RENDER](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-render) 1 — the render path never traverses the graph, One-way flow makes it structurally impossible for a camera position to change results
- **Cons:** Requires extract, retained render state, spatially scoped change signals and a spatial index over the stack, Every processing operator must tolerate an edit node appearing anywhere upstream, Enumerated point-set edits still need an identity mechanism, deferred to a separate specification

### Edits are a privileged overlay the spatial access layer applies when producing batches; processing operators never see them as nodes (rejected)

- **Pros:** Much smaller blast radius: no extract, no graph traversal from the render path, The renderer already talks to the spatial access layer directly, so edits are visible for free, Processing operators see edited data and need no awareness of editing at all
- **Cons:** Two mutation models coexist: edits, and operators that change attributes, An edit can never be placed between two processing steps — the gesture is inexpressible, Undo, history and reordering need bespoke machinery instead of reusing the graph's
- **Rejected because:** Chosen only because the render-latency obligation appeared to rule out the graph, and extract shows it does not. Once the renderer consumes a derived snapshot, this option and the accepted one behave identically at runtime — so its supposed advantage evaporates while its costs remain: two mutation models, bespoke undo, and no way to interleave an edit with a processing step.

### Edits are nodes in the document graph, and the renderer traverses that graph directly with no snapshot (rejected)

- **Pros:** One representation, no extract boundary, no synchronisation to reason about, No possibility of the render view diverging from the document
- **Cons:** Puts planner traversal inside the frame budget, violating [RFC-0006:C-RENDER](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-render) 1, Planning cost is a function of user-controlled pipeline complexity and so unbounded, Nothing prevents render-side level-of-detail choices from reaching authoritative evaluation
- **Rejected because:** It couples an interactive deadline to an operation with no deadline, which is exactly what [RFC-0006:C-RENDER](../rfc/RFC-0006.md#rfc-0006c-render) exists to forbid. The failure mode is a viewport that stalls while the camera moves, worsening as the user builds a longer pipeline.

### Destructive editing: materialise the edited cloud, or rewrite the source in place (rejected)

- **Pros:** Simplest possible model, and what CloudCompare users already expect, No stack to evaluate, no consolidation, no divergence between document and data
- **Cons:** Rewriting a remote COPC is impossible; rewriting a local one destroys the original, COPC nodes are LAZ-compressed chunks, so modification means recompression and hierarchy rewriting, Materialising the edited cloud abandons out-of-core, the project's entire premise
- **Rejected because:** Directly contradicts [RFC-0002:C-MEMORY](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-memory) and the reason the project exists. It also makes every edit irreversible and forecloses provenance entirely, since a rewritten file carries no record of what it used to be.
